At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Compliance | North America Claims, Claims Shared Services-

AXIS is seeking a Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and Audit, North America Claims to join the Claims Shared Services team. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance and Compliance, Claims Shared Services, this role will lead, oversee, enhance and optimize the North America claim direct handle, manager quality review and TPA oversight audit program. The role will also coordinate, oversee, and enhance the North America Claims SIU and Fraud program.

The successful candidate will plan, coordinate, monitor, and report on audits and quality file reviews across North America Claims, including specialty claim handler audits across multiple lines of business, TPA oversight audits, and leadership quality control file reviews. The role will manage audit execution through internal stakeholders and external audit partners, track findings through closure, report results to leadership, and use audit insights to strengthen claim handling quality, compliance, consistency, and operational performance.

This role is ideal for a claims, audit, quality assurance, or compliance professional with strong technical claims judgment, experience assessing specialty claim handler performance, working knowledge of TPA or outsourced claims partner oversight, and the ability to translate audit and file review results into practical actions that improve claim outcomes.

The successful Candidate will be responsible for:

Claims Audit Program Management
• Lead and report on the North America claim handler audit program, TPA oversight audit program, and leadership quality control file review program across multiple lines of business.
• Manage end-to-end audit execution, including planning, scope, scheduling, sample selection, file collection, stakeholder communications, and audit readiness.
• Coordinate with claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, audit vendors, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, and Operations to ensure consistent, timely audit delivery.
• Enhance audit standards, questionnaires, scorecards, and methodologies in line with claim best practices, regulatory expectations, and technical excellence standards.
• Review audit observations across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation management, settlement strategy, documentation quality, compliance, and claim handling controls.
• Track findings, action plans, remediation activities, owner accountability, due dates, and closure evidence.

Audit Results, Analytics, and Reporting
• Gather, validate, and analyze audit results, quality assurance data, compliance findings, and technical claim handling trends.
• Develop dashboards, scorecards, and management reports covering quality review results, technical audit outcomes, recurring themes, risk areas, trends, and improvement opportunities.
• Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting for Claims leadership and governance forums, covering claim handler audit results, TPA oversight audit results, and leadership quality control file review outcomes.
• Measure audit effectiveness, remediation progress, transparency, accountability, and control discipline.

Compliance, Controls, and Remediation
• Partner with Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Claims Operations, and Claims Leadership to align audit activity with regulatory, governance, and operational risk priorities.
• Monitor findings related to Medicare, regulatory obligations, documentation standards, claim handling controls, and other compliance requirements.
• Maintain action plans that address findings, strengthen controls, and promote consistent claim handling across North America specialty claim teams, TPA claim programs, and leadership quality control file reviews.
• Escalate material issues, recurring trends, control gaps, and remediation delays to appropriate leaders and governance forums.

SIU and Fraud Audit Program
• Enhance, measure, and report on the SIU and fraud deliverable program as part of the North America claims audit program.
• Assess whether SIU and fraud deliverables are timely, complete, consistent, and aligned with claim handling expectations, regulatory obligations, and technical audit standards.
• Identify themes, control gaps, escalation issues, documentation weaknesses, and opportunities to improve fraud identification, referral quality, and SIU oversight.
• Partner with SIU, Compliance, Claims leadership, TPAs, and audit vendors to strengthen execution, reporting, accountability, and remediation follow-through.

Technical Excellence and Continuous Improvement
• Use audit and quality control file review insights to improve technical claim quality, consistency, reserving discipline, litigation management, settlement practices, and compliance execution.
• Support updates to claims guidelines, audit protocols, procedures, workflows, controls, and training materials based on audit trends and root-cause analysis.
• Provide practical recommendations to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPAs, and business partners to improve claim outcomes and audit performance.
• Participate in governance meetings, working groups, and initiatives related to claims quality, audit readiness, and technical excellence.

Stakeholder Management
• Build effective relationships across North America Claims, specialty claim teams, TPAs, Compliance, Legal, Internal Audit, Actuarial, Finance, Operations, and Shared Services.
• Manage day-to-day coordination with external audit vendors, including schedules, deliverables, issue tracking, reporting inputs, and performance expectations.
• Provide audit and quality assurance subject matter support to claim leaders, specialty claim handlers, TPA managers, and governance stakeholders.
• Communicate findings, themes, risks, and recommendations clearly to management and senior leadership.

Skills
• 6–10 years of experience in commercial P&C insurance, reinsurance, specialty claims, claims audit, quality assurance, compliance, operational risk, or a related discipline.
• Minimum 3 years of experience supporting or managing claims audits, quality assurance reviews, compliance monitoring, operational controls, or remediation tracking.
• Experience working with TPAs, outsourced claims partners, audit vendors, or vendor oversight programs.
• Experience auditing specialty claim files across multiple lines of business and supporting technical claim quality reviews.
• Experience developing audit reports, dashboards, metrics, scorecards, or performance analytics for leadership review.
• Strong technical claims judgment and ability to assess claim handling quality across coverage, liability, damages, reserving, litigation, settlement, and documentation practices.
• Strong analytical, communication, project coordination, organizational, stakeholder management, and vendor management skills.
• Ability to identify themes, root causes, risks, control gaps, performance improvement opportunities, and remediation priorities.
• Ability to manage multiple audits, stakeholders, priorities, and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and reporting tools.
• Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree, CPCU, AIC, ARM, CFE, CIA, CPA, JD, or other relevant professional designation preferred.

Additional Information

• Ability to work in a hybrid environment (3 days in office)
• Some travel may be required

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of 140-160K. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is [Exempt/Non-Exempt] for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:

We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

Senior Talent Acquisition Partner

Job Family Grouping: HR Group
Job Family: Talent Acquisition

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in shaping the talent behind AXIS’ continued growth and transformation.

The Senior Talent Acquisition Partner supports several of AXIS’ most strategically important functions, including Business Technology Services (BTS), Data & Analytics, Global Operations and Transformation. This role serves as a trusted talent advisor to business leaders, helping attract, assess and hire critical talent while providing market intelligence, talent insights and recruitment strategy guidance that supports business objectives.

The successful candidate will partner closely with hiring managers, People Business Partners and executive stakeholders to solve complex hiring challenges, build diverse talent pipelines and deliver an exceptional experience for both candidates and hiring teams.

What will you do in this role?

  • Partner closely with hiring managers, People Business Partners and business leaders to understand hiring needs, business priorities, workforce plans and talent requirements.
  • Lead full-cycle recruitment activity for assigned roles, including intake discussions, sourcing strategy, candidate identification, screening, assessment, offer management and onboarding handoff.
  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies across multiple channels including internal mobility, referrals, direct sourcing, talent communities, external outreach, agencies and recruiting platforms.
  • Serve as a trusted talent advisor by providing talent market intelligence, competitive hiring insights, compensation perspective, talent availability analysis and recommendations to support informed hiring decisions.
  • Partner with hiring managers on search calibration, helping define realistic and competitive hiring criteria based on market conditions and available talent pools.
  • Build and maintain pipelines of talent for recurring and business-critical skill sets across technology, data, analytics, operations and transformation functions.
  • Deliver a high-quality candidate and hiring manager experience through consistent communication, thoughtful guidance and proactive issue resolution throughout the recruitment process.
  • Conduct candidate assessments and evaluate qualifications, capabilities, experiences and alignment with organizational values and role expectations.
  • Guide hiring managers through structured interviewing, candidate evaluation and selection decisions that promote consistency and sound hiring practices.
  • Lead offer strategy discussions and negotiations in partnership with hiring managers, People Business Partners, Compensation and other stakeholders as appropriate.
  • Monitor pipeline health, recruitment activity and key hiring metrics to identify risks, opportunities and process improvements.
  • Support workforce planning discussions by identifying talent trends, competitive intelligence and external market dynamics relevant to future hiring needs.
  • Manage relationships with external search firms, recruitment agencies and other service providers, ensuring effective utilization and alignment with AXIS standards.
  • Participate in Talent Acquisition initiatives related to recruiting technology, candidate experience, reporting, sourcing effectiveness, process improvement and hiring manager enablement.
  • Mentor and support other recruiting professionals by sharing best practices, market insights and recruiting expertise.
  • Apply sound judgment when navigating complex searches, shifting business priorities and challenging talent market conditions.

You may also be required to take on additional duties, responsibilities and activities appropriate to the nature of this role.

About You

We encourage you to bring your own experience and expertise to the table. While certain qualifications are important, we are open to discussing how your unique knowledge, perspective and capabilities can contribute to success in this role.

What you need to have

  • 7+ years of corporate or in-house full-cycle Talent Acquisition experience supporting professional, technical, operational and/or corporate functions.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple concurrent searches, priorities and stakeholder groups in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience partnering directly with hiring managers, business leaders and HR stakeholders to develop and execute recruitment strategies.
  • Demonstrated success sourcing, engaging and hiring passive candidates through a variety of channels and sourcing methodologies.
  • Strong understanding of talent acquisition best practices, candidate assessment, sourcing strategies and recruitment lifecycle management.
  • Experience using recruiting metrics, talent market data and pipeline insights to inform hiring decisions and recruitment strategy.
  • Experience recruiting for specialized, hard-to-fill or business-critical positions.
  • Strong communication, consulting and relationship management skills with the ability to influence and build credibility across stakeholder groups.
  • Experience leading candidate offer discussions and supporting compensation negotiations.
  • Proficiency using applicant tracking systems, recruiting technologies, sourcing tools and recruiting analytics platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage confidential information appropriately.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment and adapt effectively to changing business needs.
  • Demonstrated commitment to delivering an exceptional candidate and hiring manager experience.

What we prefer you to have

  • Experience recruiting for technology, business technology, software engineering, cyber security, infrastructure, cloud, data, analytics, operations, transformation or change-management related roles.
  • Experience supporting technology organizations, operations organizations or enterprise transformation initiatives.
  • Experience recruiting within insurance, reinsurance, financial services or another highly regulated industry.
  • Experience supporting executive-level, highly specialized or difficult-to-fill searches.
  • Experience using talent intelligence, market mapping, competitive research or workforce analytics to inform recruiting strategies.
  • Experience supporting global stakeholders and multi-region recruitment activity.
  • Experience mentoring recruiters, leading projects or driving Talent Acquisition best practices.
  • Experience partnering with executive leaders and senior business stakeholders.
  • Experience with Workday Recruiting, LinkedIn Recruiter and other modern recruiting technologies.
  • Exposure to AI-enabled recruiting tools, talent intelligence platforms or recruiting automation solutions.
  • Interest in continuous improvement, recruitment innovation and data-driven decision making.

Role Factors

In this role, you will typically be required to:

Be in the office 3 days per week

What we offer

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $130,000 to $162,000 (NY). Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and much more.

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How does this role contribute to our collective success?

The Head of Insights & Analytics leads a multidisciplinary team that transforms data into actionable insights and measurable business value. You will be accountable for enterprise reporting, business intelligence, performance analytics, insight generation, analytics strategy, and business adoption of analytical solutions.

The role identifies and prioritizes opportunities where advanced analytics and AI can drive business value and partners with Data Science & AI Delivery leadership to ensure successful execution.

The role’s purpose is to ensure the business gets the right solutions for the right needs, whether that’s a dashboard, a predictive model, an AI-driven tool or an agentic solution, always focused on delivering optimal business outcomes rather than analytics for its own sake. This is a high-impact leadership role, requiring a blend of strategic vision, technical acumen, and exceptional people leadership to drive a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and business partnership.

What will you do in this role?

  • Lead a High-Performing Analytics Function: Build, inspire, and manage a multidisciplinary team (spanning BI/reporting analysts, and data analysts) to deliver insights and analytics to AXIS in support of the business’ goals. Strategically lead the Data Science & AI Delivery team to leverage with Data Science & AI Delivery leadership to leverage specialized AI and data science capability. Cultivate a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

  • Drive Outcome-Focused Delivery: Work with business leaders across underwriting, claims, finance, operations, and other functions to understand how analytics and AI can support and enable their goals. Own prioritization, funding alignment, value realization, and adoption of analytical capabilities across the business. Act as the executive sponsor for analytics and AI initiatives. Ensure the team delivers practical solutions that drive decision-making and measurable improvements – prioritizing business outcomes over output volume.

  • Advanced Analytics, Data Science & AI Delivery: Define business priorities, success metrics, governance requirements, and expected outcomes for advanced analytics and AI initiatives. Execute with the Data Science & AI Delivery team, who are accountable for technical design, model development, deployment, and operationalization. Ensure business value realization and organizational adoption following implementation. Champion the selection of the right analytical approach (e.g., diagnostic analysis, predictive modelling, machine learning, AI automation) to solve each business problem, ensuring solutions are fit-for-purpose and add tangible value (e.g., improved loss ratio, enhanced customer experience, operational efficiency).

  • Traditional Insights & Management Information: Oversee development and enhancement of dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators (KPIs) that provide a single source of truth. Ensure reporting is accurate, timely, and clearly communicates insights to business stakeholders for areas like underwriting performance, claims trends, customer insights, and financial metrics.

  • Strategic Planning & Vision: Define and communicate a clear vision and roadmap for the Insights & Analytics function, aligned with the company’s strategy. Identify opportunities to leverage emerging tools and methods to continuously advance analytical capabilities in a pragmatic way.

  • Stakeholder Engagement & Consulting: Act as a trusted partner to business leaders. Translate complex data science and analytics concepts into clear, actionable business insights.   • Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with other Data & Analytics functions, working as one team to ensure the best possible end-to-end outcomes are delivered for the business.

  • Governance & Best Practices: In partnership with the Data and AI Governance team, establish standards and best practices for analytics and reporting, including data quality control, model governance, and ethical AI use. Ensure adherence to regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to insurance data and models. Promote data-driven decision-making and champion data literacy across the organization.

  • Analytics Operating Model & Governance: Establish and maintain enterprise standards for reporting, KPI definition, insight generation, business performance measurement, and analytics prioritization. Ensure AI and advanced analytics initiatives align with business strategy and governance requirements.

  • Performance Management: Define and track key performance indicators for the Insights & Analytics function. Ensure work is prioritized for maximum impact, resources are allocated effectively, and projects are delivered on time and within budget.

Success Measures / Key Outcomes

  • Business Impact of Insights: Demonstrable improvements in business outcomes fueled by analytics (e.g., improved underwriting decisions, reduced claims leakage, increased revenue) due to insights and models delivered by the team.

  • Continuous Improvement: Establishment of improved processes and practices that increase the speed, quality, and reliability of analytics delivery.

jobs.title: Data Insights Lead - Reserving
jobs.description_html:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance.  We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture.  As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work. 

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

How This Role Contributes to Our Collective Success?

This is an opportunity to use data and analytics to make a meaningful difference to one of the most important decision-making areas at AXIS: Reserving. In this role, you will help the Reserving team turn complex data into clear, trusted insight so they can better understand trends, explain movements, and make confident decisions.

In this role, you will help us:

  • Make reserving decisions easier to understand by improving access to consistent, timely, and well-defined data.

  • Bring important trends to the surface, helping the team understand what is changing, why it matters, and where more analysis may be needed.

  • Reduce manual effort and improve the way reserving analysis is produced, shared, and used across the business.


You will help shape how reserving analytics evolves at AXIS, building practical insight capabilities that make it easier to understand portfolio movements, compare views across business areas, monitor key indicators, and support high-quality discussions with senior stakeholders.
 

You will work closely with colleagues across Reserving, Finance, Actuarial, Claims, Underwriting, and Data & Analytics to understand what the Reserving team needs and turn those needs into useful dashboards, datasets, self-service tools, and repeatable insight products. You will also partner with technical teams to make sure reserving data is trusted, accessible, clearly defined, and fit for decision-making.

Key Responsibilities
 

Be a Trusted Partner to the Reserving Team

  • Build strong relationships with the Reserving team and the wider teams that use reserving information, taking time to understand their processes, challenges, priorities, and decision-making needs.

  • Help define the reserving analytics roadmap, making sure the work we prioritise delivers clear value for the Reserving team and the business.


Create Better Data Products and Insight Tools

  • Design and deliver dashboards, datasets, and self-service tools that give the Reserving team clearer views of loss development, claims experience, exposure changes, prior-year development, and other important indicators.

  • Replace static, manual reporting with more interactive insight solutions that help users explore trends, compare results, test assumptions, and identify areas for deeper review.

  • Help identify, explain and monitor reserve signals, including AvE, PYD, claims emergence, large loss activity, exposure/mix changes and reserve diagnostics.


Explore Modern Analytics and AI

  • Work with actuarial, data science, and AI colleagues to explore where modern analytics can support reserving analysis, scenario exploration, anomaly detection, and clearer explanation of key drivers.

  • Promote practical and responsible use of AI and analytics, with a focus on improving speed, transparency, and confidence while maintaining strong governance and actuarial judgement.


Inspire Through Insight

  • Create clear, intuitive visualizations that help colleagues understand reserving movements, emerging trends, portfolio changes, and areas of uncertainty.

  • Help improve how reserving insights are communicated so they are concise, consistent, and useful for actuarial, finance, management, and business discussions.


Set Standards for Excellence

  • Help define clear standards for reserving metrics, data definitions, reporting, reconciliation, and interpretation of key indicators.

  • Support high-quality, governed outputs that align with enterprise data standards, actuarial controls, and financial reporting needs.


Collaborate Across D&A

  • Collaborate with architecture, engineering, governance, finance, actuarial, claims, and underwriting colleagues so reserving needs are considered from the data foundation through to the final insight experience.

  • Look for opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual data wrangling, and build reusable insight capabilities that teams can rely on over time.

You may also be asked to take on additional responsibilities aligned with the nature and scope of this role.


About You
 

Required Experience & Skills

  • Experience in data, analytics, actuarial, finance, or a related insurance or reinsurance role.

  • Experience helping to design, improve, or deliver data and analytics solutions for business users.

  • A deep understanding of insurance or reinsurance data, including how claims, policy, exposure, premium, underwriting, finance, and actuarial information can be used to support analysis.

  • The ability to lead through influence, work with technical teams, and bring people together around a shared outcome.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to make complex data and analysis clear, practical, and actionable.

  • Experience creating dashboards, datasets, visualizations, or self-service tools that help business users understand performance, trends, and drivers.

  • Curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, and an interest in applying them to real business problems in a practical and responsible way.

  • Familiarity with data visualization tools such as Power BI, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with reserving, actuarial, finance, claims, underwriting, or performance reporting teams.

  • Some knowledge of reserving processes, actuarial triangles, loss development, claims trends, or financial close reporting.

  • Hands-on experience with Power BI and other visualization platforms.


What Really Sets You Apart

  • You enjoy turning complex data into insight that people can trust, understand, and use.

  • You are naturally curious and like asking how analysis could be faster, clearer, more consistent, and more useful.

  • You are excited by the chance to help modernize reserving analytics at AXIS and build tools that improve confidence, transparency, and business understanding.

Role Factors


In this role, you will typically be required to:

  • Attend your local office at least three (3) days per week to meet and build relationships with colleagues and the wider business.

  • Engage in company activities to grow your network and build a strong team culture.

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $150,000 - $200,000 (New York) Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location. 

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more.  

Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Medical Only Claims Representative
jobs.description_html:
Summit provides independent insurance agents and their clients with market-leading workers’ comp insurance and elite customer service. We’re growing and currently serve more than 7,000 independent agents and 31,000 policyholders across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic.

Our strength comes from a single-minded focus on workers’ comp and a commitment to long-term customer relationships. Summit is who you turn to when you need a specialist who not only knows workers’ comp but also gets to know your business and your priorities.

Our field team members are located in every state in which we operate.

Summit is a member of the Great American Insurance Group where our highest goal is for all employees to feel included, respected, and empowered to perform at their best.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities

  • Manages an inventory of claims to evaluate compensability/liability.
  • Conducts claim investigations to confirm coverage and to determine liability, compensability and damages.
  • Determines and may negotiate appropriate claim settlements/reserves within prescribed authority. May attend arbitrations, mediations, depositions, or trials.
  • Conveys routine to moderately complex information regarding coverage and settlements to insureds, claimants, and external partners.
  • May authorize payments in accordance with assigned authority limit and ensures payments are made in a timely manner.
  • Maintains accurate and detailed claim files, including all correspondence, reports, and settlement agreements.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • This role is remote in Illinois.

Job Requirements

Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Risk Management and Insurance, Finance, or a related field or equivalent experience.

Experience: Generally, a minimum of 6 months of experience in property and casualty claims handling. Completion of or continuing progress toward a professional designation preferred, such as Associate in Claims (AIC).


Scope of Job/Qualifications: Works within specific limits and authority on assignments of moderate technical complexity and coordination. Demonstrates functional analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills. Demonstrates knowledge of insurance policies, coverage, and claims handling procedures. Develops and maintains knowledge of industry laws and regulations. Demonstrates ability to organize and prioritize caseloads, ensuring timely resolution of claims. Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to build relationships and handle negotiations. Proven ability to handle confidential information with discretion.



Company:

SCI Summit Consulting, LLC


Salary Range:

$56,400.00 -$75,600.00

Benefits:

We offer competitive benefits packages for full-time and part-time employees*. Full-time employees have access to medical, dental, and vision coverage, wellness plans, parental leave, adoption assistance, and tuition reimbursement. Full-time and eligible part-time employees also enjoy Paid Time Off and paid holidays, a 401(k) plan with company match, an employee stock purchase plan, and commuter benefits.

Compensation varies by role, level, and location and is influenced by skills, experience, and business needs. Your recruiter will provide details about benefits and specific compensation ranges during the hiring process. Learn more at http://www.gaig.com/careers.

*Excludes seasonal employees and interns.

Requirements

  • Experience in configuring, deploying, and troubleshooting various business critical applications
  • Experience in both Windows and Linux Server OS
  • Experience deploying and maintaining SaaS Applications
  • Moderate to advanced scripting or programing experience. PowerShell required. Python is a plus.
  • Experience with automation tooling and practices
  • Experience maintaining relationships and coordinating with vendors and third parties
  • Well versed in Enterprise Networking. Familiar with firewall concepts, subnetting, and other enterprise Networking systems.

  • Ability to troubleshoot various business applications.
  • Functional experience with multiple enterprise technologies and applications.
  • Moderate Powershell experience. Additional scripting languages preferred.
  • VmWare and vSAN
  • System Center Configuration Manager administration, deployments, and updates.
  • Web Infrastructure (IBM Websphere, IIS, F5)
  • Redhat Linux is a plus.
  • Centralized logging and monitoring.
  • Expert level knowledge of Windows Server Environments.

jobs.title: Territory Sales Manager- Personal Auto- New Mexico
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

Job Title: Territory Sales Manager

Job Summary: Our Territory Sales Managers are responsible for driving profitable growth in their assigned territory. We are looking for motivated team players who can influence independent agents to sell Hallmark Auto and Renters products, develop existing and new agency relationships, generate production growth and execute business plans to meet the companies’ sales expectations.  A successful Territory Sales Manager will be able to accomplish this through communication with sales and product leadership, prospecting new opportunities, agency appointments, visits to existing agencies and through other field sales activities.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for managing and developing a territory of independent agents, including finding new agency partners and maintaining strong relationships with agents at all levels within the agencies.
  • Implement and execute sales strategies to achieve sales goals.
  • Drives new business policy and premium growth.
  • Assess agency mix of business, retention and profitability results.
  • Responsible for agency onboarding and training regarding Hallmark products and best practices such as company underwriting guidelines, programs, websites and rating tools.
  • Must be able to effectively present and communicate to large groups and influence behavior through consultive selling.
  • Required to evaluate agency relationships for profitability.
  • Attend and participate in industry conventions, events or groups associations.
  • Communicate industry trends, competitor changes and observations and feedback on existing products and market opportunities.
  • Maintain up to date records of field activity, contact information, sales strategy and new agency appointment paperwork and other critical reports and documentation.
  • This position is a field sales role and requires regular travel throughout the assigned territory with an expectation of 30% overnight travel

Qualifications for the Territory Sales Manager:

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree preferred or Experience of 3-5 years insurance sales experience
  • Experience: A working knowledge of non-standard auto insurance operations: claims, coverage, products and underwriting are preferable to effectively communicate with agency and company personnel
  • Skills:
    • Bi-Lingual (English and Spanish) is preferred
    • Proficient in Microsoft Office Applications
    • Excellent Communication and Interpersonal Skills
    • Organization and Time Management
    • Ability to analyze and interpret report data through spreadsheets. Must be able to interpret statistical data from company records and build action plans around insights
    • Problem Solving Skills
    • Must be flexible in nature and highly motivated self-starter

Hallmark Financial Services is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

 Required to evaluate agency relationships for profitability.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager, Personal Lines- TEXAS
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

Regional Sales Manager – Texas

Position Summary

The Regional Sales Manager is responsible for management of a collection of states/territories and Territory Managers consistent with the companies’ goals. This position is accountable to growing premium volume with profitable loss ratios, achieving sales and production objectives through new and existing agency relationships, and ensuring effective execution of the Company's sales strategy.

The Regional Sales Manager serves as the primary leader and resource for Territory Sales Managers, providing direction, coaching, performance management, and support while partnering closely with the Sales Director and cross-functional leadership.

This position is requires regular travel throughout Texas to support agency relationships, team activities, and business development.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Management

  • Directly manage, coach, and develop team members including hiring, onboarding and all aspects of performance management.
  • Establish clear performance expectations and hold TSMs accountable for achieving sales, growth, profitability, and agency development objectives.
  • Conduct regular one-on-one meetings, performance reviews, and territory business reviews. Activities will include field visits/ride-alongs.
  • Identify training and development opportunities and create plans to strengthen individual and team capabilities.
  • Foster a collaborative, accountable, and results-driven sales culture.
  • Manage travel and other expenses to stay within budgetary constraints.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of the region’s non-standard personal auto insurance market. Monitor and provide leadership competitor activity, market trends, regulatory developments, and changes within the independent agency distribution channel.

Sales & Business Development

  • Develop and execute sales strategies aligned with company objectives and underwriting appetite. Identify opportunities to increase market penetration and improve the company's competitive position.
  • Monitor territory production performance, new business, retention, loss ratio and other key performance indicators. Identify opportunities for profitable growth or improvement.
  • Assist Sales Director and AVP of Sales/Marketing with specific strategies, research, market analysis and annual planning and budgeting. Assist with sales forecasting, budgeting, and business planning.
  • Partner with TSMs to develop territory-specific business plans and strategies.
  • Review sales reports and performance data to identify trends, opportunities, and areas requiring corrective action.
  • Support the identification and development of new agency relationships and distribution opportunities.
  • Work with TSMs to strengthen relationships with key agencies and producers.
  • Actively participate in regular Territory Manager producer meetings/and or conference calls, share competitor information, assist with training and contribute to department goals and planning, attend industry events and be the primary point of contact for regional large agency groups. 
  • Serve as an escalation point for significant agency or producer issues.
  • Create and maintain structure to appropriately execute agency appointments, terminations and updates. Create and implement programs to improve loss ratio, retention, quote volume, sales conversion and brand recognition.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Underwriting to ensure sales activities align with company risk appetite and profitability objectives.
  • Collaborate with Claims, Marketing, Product, Operations, and other departments to address market and agency needs. Provide field feedback to help inform business and product decisions.
  • Communicate company initiatives, programs, and strategic priorities to the TSM team.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Insurance, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in insurance sales, preferably personal auto or non-standard personal auto.
  • 2+ years of experience managing, coaching, or leading sales professionals.
  • Demonstrated success achieving sales and business development objectives.
  • Strong understanding of independent insurance agency distribution.
  • Strong knowledge of the Texas insurance market.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to travel regularly throughout Texas.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

Preferred

  • Experience specifically in non-standard personal auto insurance.
  • Established relationships with Texas independent insurance agencies and producers.
  • Experience managing geographically dispersed sales professionals.
  • Insurance designation such as CIC, CPCU, or similar.

Hallmark Financial Services is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Senior Bodily Injury Claims Adjuster, Personal Lines
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties assigned as needed.

  • Act as point-of-contact for insureds regarding general claim questions and reporting of claims.
  • Identify and perform coverage analysis and prepare reservation of rights/declination letters when appropriate.
  • Make liability decisions, analyze aggravating factors and potential for shared responsibility, and set up subrogation (as applicable)
  • Manage and work with defense counsel (as applicable) to develop the case to include expert support and case strategy.
  • Conduct proper reviews and independent investigations pre-litigation.
  • Maintain cases on diary to ensure proper file management, evaluation, strategy, and timely reserve recommendations are handled.
  • Keep current running notes to reflect file development and ensure proper documents are maintained in the claims system.
  • Prioritize and evaluate claims, the majority will be injury/casualty with attorney involvement
  • Negotiate claim settlements with plaintiff counsel as indicated, or issue denials to claimant/claimant attorney as appropriate.
  • Use knowledge of state regulatory and statutory requirements for a multi-state region
  • May also handle multi-compete/complex property claims and renters injury claims

Qualifications to perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Education and/or Experience: Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university; or 1-5 years related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience handling attorney represented bodily injury (BI/UM/UIM) exposures in a personal lines claim’s environment
  • Experience handling physical damage exposures in a personal lines claims environment
  • Detailed oriented with the ability to work in a team environment and be flexible to daily changing needs and job duties
  • Ability to analyze and problem solve, working closely with others to coordinate and complete projects
  • Ability to think critically and resolve problems of varying complexity
  • Ability to perform with minimal supervision
  • Self-motivated with a strong work ethic
  • Excellent oral, written and interpersonal communication skills
  • Must be customer service oriented, highly organized and efficient
  • Effective Computer Skills
  • Advanced Microsoft Office Skills
  • Ability to learn multiple software applications
  • Must obtain applicable adjusters license(s) by state within 3 months of start date

Preferred Skills

  • Auto bodily injury attorney represented and/or litigation experience
  • Multiple language skills a plus
  • TX Adjuster License

jobs.title: AVP, Commercial Sales and Marketing
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

AVP, Commercial Lines Sales & Marketing is responsible for leading Hallmark Commercial’s sales and marketing efforts, with a primary focus on expanding the company’s distribution footprint through the prospecting, recruitment, and appointment of established Commercial P&C agencies. This role provides strategic leadership, manages the Sales & Marketing team, and partners across departments to drive profitable growth.

Job Duties

Develop and manage sales and marketing activities that promote the brand and effectively communicate HCI’s product appetite and business objectives.

Prospect, identify, and recruit established Commercial P&C agencies with strong production potential and alignment with HCI’s appetite. Build relationships with agency principals and Commercial Lines leaders, evaluate prospective agencies, and develop a pipeline of qualified new appointments.

Conduct agency visits and presentations, manage prospects through appointment and onboarding, and track prospecting activity, appointments, and production in Salesforce to expand HCI’s presence in targeted markets.

Partner with HCI leadership to identify profitable target markets, define sales and engagement metrics, and develop and execute marketing plans that support growth and profitability objectives.

Lead agency management efforts, including performance tracking, rehabilitation plans, termination of underperforming agents, and identification and engagement of new agents in alignment with strategic objectives.

Establish sales objectives and minimum performance criteria for commercial sales staff; coordinate sales and service efforts to achieve maximum results. Provides coaching and mentorship to direct reports.

Manage HCI Elite Agent partnership activities, including regular engagement, quarterly performance reviews, and planning an annual Elite agent event.

Track market and competitor trends; communicate relevant market intel to HCI Leadership includng changes in product offerings, rates, competitor entrants or exists, etc.

Develop deep working knowledgeable of HCI’s commercial underwriting appetite, guidelines, and policy coverage language.

Collaborate with Agency Licensing and Compliance team to optimize agency appointment and maintenance processes.

Communicate regularly with HCI Leadership, Underwriting, Claims, and Licensing personnel, as needed.

Other duties as may be assigned.

Independence

This position provides a high level of independence. The individual performing this job should be confident in his/her decision-making abilities and have a general understanding of when issues should be brought to Leadership or Human Resources.

Supervision

  • Supervises 2-4 direct reports, including Business Development Representatives

Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring and training employees; planning, assigning and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Education, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills: 

  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university; or equivalent experience or training.
  • Prior Commercial Lines sales and marketing experience with a successful track record required.
  • Continuing education with certificates in CPCU, ARM or other similar industry designations preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Salesforce preferred
  • Strong working knowledge of Commercial P&C products including knowledge of coverage provided for all commercial lines of business.
  • Basic knowledge of standard agent contracts, commission levels, and profit share schemes offered in the industry.
  • Knowledge of agency management metrics and the ability to analyze relative data, draw appropriate conclusions and develop actionable items from the data.
  • Ability to build internal/external relationships and develop long-term strategic partnerships.
  • Ability to work in a team environment and be flexible to daily changing needs and job duties.
  • Ability to analyze and solve problems by working closely with others to coordinate and complete projects.
  • Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Proficient Microsoft Office Skills and competent understanding of company specific systems and tools.
  • Occasional overnight travel required

Hallmark Financial Services is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Territory Sales Manager- Personal Auto
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

Job Title: Territory Sales Manager

Job Summary: Our Territory Sales Managers are responsible for driving profitable growth in their assigned territory. We are looking for motivated team players who can influence independent agents to sell Hallmark Auto and Renters products, develop existing and new agency relationships, generate production growth and execute business plans to meet the companies’ sales expectations.  A successful Territory Sales Manager will be able to accomplish this through communication with sales and product leadership, prospecting new opportunities, agency appointments, visits to existing agencies and through other field sales activities.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for managing and developing a territory of independent agents, including finding new agency partners and maintaining strong relationships with agents at all levels within the agencies.
  • Implement and execute sales strategies to achieve sales goals.
  • Drives new business policy and premium growth.
  • Assess agency mix of business, retention and profitability results.
  • Responsible for agency onboarding and training regarding Hallmark products and best practices such as company underwriting guidelines, programs, websites and rating tools.
  • Must be able to effectively present and communicate to large groups and influence behavior through consultive selling.
  • Required to evaluate agency relationships for profitability.
  • Attend and participate in industry conventions, events or groups associations.
  • Communicate industry trends, competitor changes and observations and feedback on existing products and market opportunities.
  • Maintain up to date records of field activity, contact information, sales strategy and new agency appointment paperwork and other critical reports and documentation.
  • This position is a field sales role and requires regular travel throughout the assigned territory with an expectation of 30% overnight travel

Qualifications for the Territory Sales Manager:

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree preferred or Experience of 3-5 years insurance sales experience
  • Experience: A working knowledge of non-standard auto insurance operations: claims, coverage, products and underwriting are preferable to effectively communicate with agency and company personnel
  • Skills:
    • Bi-Lingual (English and Spanish) is preferred
    • Proficient in Microsoft Office Applications
    • Excellent Communication and Interpersonal Skills
    • Organization and Time Management
    • Ability to analyze and interpret report data through spreadsheets. Must be able to interpret statistical data from company records and build action plans around insights
    • Problem Solving Skills
    • Must be flexible in nature and highly motivated self-starter

Hallmark Financial Services is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Material Damage Appraiser
jobs.description_html:
Job Description:

Position Summary:

  • Provides service to all customers and anticipates their need for communication, results and action.
  • Responsible for the prompt, accurate and efficient appraisal and payment of vehicle repair damage and vehicle total loss values, from moderate to severe damage, on all types of vehicles, while exercising independent decision making skills and judgment.

Essential Functions:

  • Receives assignment from Claim Representatives electronically on all types of vehicles.
  • Determines best course of action with regards to vehicle damage evaluation (i.e. Desk review, shop estimate/photo review)
  • Using the documentation available, determines the extent of damage and whether the vehicle is repairable or not economical to repair.
  • Verifies the damage to the vehicle is related to the loss facts given by the Claims Representative.
  • Changes reserves, negotiate agreed repair costs with shops, determines total loss vehicle values and issues payment.
  • Requests photos from owner or shop for in order to write an estimate/supplement or redline a shop estimate/supplement.
  • Contacts customers and shops to setup appraisal appointments.
  • Uploads all work product into the claim and the dispatch system.
  • Documents all correspondence, discussions and decisions in the ACD or claim file.
  • Works closely with Casualty and Auto Physical Damage personnel toward the successful adjustment of first and third party physical damage claims.
  • Notifies the Total Loss Claim Representative of total loss vehicles and, when appropriate, moves the salvage to Copart or other storage free places.
  • Provides guidance to other Claims personnel, assists in their training when asked. Occasionally gives technical direction and authority when requested by Team Manager.
  • Provides quality service to all customers.
  • Any other tasks or responsibilities assigned

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of vehicle construction, repair methods, and total loss valuation
  • Ability to interpret and analyze estimates, photos, and repair documentation
  • Effective negotiation skills with repair facilities and vendors
  • Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines
  • Proficiency in claims systems and standard office software
  • Customer-focused mindset with the ability to handle difficult conversations professionally

Education & Experience Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in business, automotive technology, or a related field preferred
  • Minimum of 2–5 years of experience in auto damage appraisal, auto body repair, insurance claims, or a related field
  • Prior experience handling moderate to severe vehicle damage and total loss evaluations strongly preferred
  • Experience working with estimating platforms (e.g., CCC, Mitchell, or Audatex) preferred
  • Knowledge of insurance claims handling processes and state-specific regulations preferred
  • Texas Adjuster License required

Hallmark Financial Services is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Claims Specialist
jobs.description_html:
The Workers’ Compensation Claims Specialist manages within company best practices lower-level, non-complex and non-problematic workers’ compensation claims within delegated limited authority to best possible outcome, under the direct supervision of a senior claims professional, supporting the goals of claims department and of CorVel.

This is a remote position.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Receives Workers’ Compensation claims, confirms policy coverage and acknowledgment of the claim
  • Determines validity and compensability of the claim
  • Establishes reserves and authorizes payments within reserving authority limits
  • Manages non-complex lost-time workers’ compensation claims under close supervision
  • Communicates claim status with the customer, claimant and client
  • Adheres to client and carrier guidelines and participates in claims review as needed
  • Assists other claims professionals with more complex or problematic claims as necessary
  • Additional projects and duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS: 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to learn rapidly to develop knowledge and understanding of claims practice
  • Ability to identify, analyze and solve problems
  • Computer proficiency and technical aptitude with the ability to utilize Microsoft Office including Excel spreadsheets
  • Strong interpersonal, time management and organizational skills
  • Ability to meet or exceed performance competencies
  • Ability to work both independently and within a team environment

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE: 

  • Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and related experience
  • Minimum of 1 year of industry experience and claims management preferred
  • Current license or certification in Workers’ Compensation must be maintained throughout employment with CorVel

PAY RANGE: 

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location.  Pay rates are established taking into account the following factors:  federal, state, and local minimum wage requirements, the geographic location differential, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, internal employee equity, and market conditions.  Our ranges may be modified at any time. 

For leveled roles (I, II, III, Senior, Lead, etc.) new hires may be slotted into a different level, either up or down, based on assessment during interview process taking into consideration experience, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.  The level may impact the salary range and these adjustments would be clarified during the offer process. 

Pay Range:  $52,999 – $85,473 

A list of our benefit offerings can be found on our CorVel website: CorVel Careers | Opportunities in Risk Management 

In general, our opportunities will be posted for up to 1 year from date of posting, or until we have selected candidate(s) to fulfill the opening, whichever comes first.

ABOUT CORVEL:

CorVel, a certified Great Place to Work® Company, is a national provider of industry-leading risk management solutions for the workers’ compensation, auto, health and disability management industries.   CorVel was founded in 1987 and has been publicly traded on the NASDAQ stock exchange since 1991. Our continual investment in human capital and technology enable us to deliver the most innovative and integrated solutions to our clients.  We are a stable and growing company with a strong, supportive culture and plenty of career advancement opportunities.  Over 4,000 people working across the United States embrace our core values of Accountability, Commitment, Excellence, Integrity and Teamwork (ACE-IT!). 

A comprehensive benefits package is available for full-time regular employees and includes Medical (HDHP) w/Pharmacy, Dental, Vision, Long Term Disability, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Account Options, Life Insurance, Accident Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, Pre-paid Legal Insurance, Parking and Transit FSA accounts, 401K, ROTH 401K, and paid time off.

CorVel is an Equal Opportunity Employer, drug free workplace, and complies with ADA regulations as applicable.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Nurse
jobs.description_html:
The Quality Assurance Nurse is responsible for case management quality assurance and mentorship of operations staff, providing tools and calibrating processes, while ensuring consistent delivery of CorVel’s case management services.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop, implement, and provide ongoing quality assurance calibration of processes as well as a case management mentoring, both managed and delivered at the operational level
  • Educate and equip operations with performance measurement and reporting tools that can be used to objectively measure and grow operations
  • Provide national account and regulatory quality oversight
  • As applicable, provide oversight and management of URAC compliance and renewals
  • Work with executive, general and case management department management to ensure the case management department successfully implemented and is adhering to CorVel standards (including quality assurance, reporting, and management processes)
  • Work closely with new hires to ensure consistent and full integration/training of all case management managers to CorVel standards as well as training for system usage pertaining to case management and reporting
  • Identify developmental needs and and participate in training of case management leadership, including the training/re-training of all offices on standards and procedures, and usages of the CorVel case management and reporting system
  • Develop, run and interpret management reports to ensure the case management operations are utilizing the tools available to manage compliance of services delivery within company standards
  • Facilitate peer-to-peer quality reviews to ensure delivery of quality case management
  • Review results and outcomes with general management and case management leadership and develop action plans where warranted
  • Make recommendations in collaboration with field operations to ensure actions toward improvement are identified
  • Develop and oversee case management manager mentor program to facilitate the onboarding of new supervision and management to equip field with the tools for compliance and consistency of CorVel standards and procedures
  • Implementation, oversight and communication of regulatory requirements within case management services to include, state, federal and URAC
  • Identify trends and recommend action plans to management for continuous process improvement
  • Ability to travel up to fifty percent of the time  
  • Additional duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS:

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • PC literate, including Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
  • Strong knowledge of clinical and case management processes
  • Strong knowledge and experience in quality assurance and training programs
  • Proficient in identifying case management office improvement opportunities and communicating and implementing solutions
  • Ability to remain poised in stressful situations and communicate using diplomacy
  • Ability to manage multiple complex projects and competing priorities while working under pressure to meet deadlines and maintaining strong customer service orientation
  • Effective quantitative and analytical skills
  • Must have strong organizational skills
  • Ability to work independently or in a team environment while functioning as an educator rather than an auditor
  • Knowledge of the entire claims administration, case management and cost containment solution as applicable to third party administrator operations

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Graduate of accredited school of nursing with a diploma/Associates degree (Bachelor of Science degree or Bachelor of Science in Nursing preferred)
  • 3 or more years of recent clinical experience, preferably in rehabilitation
  • National certification (CRC, CIRS, CCRN, CVE, CCM, etc.), CCM preferred
  • Four year degree from an accredited college or university preferred
  • Certified Trainer and/or Quality Assurance distinction preferred
  • Four (4) years of case management experience preferred or equivalent experience
  • Prior quality assurance and/or training a plus
  • Current RN licensure

PAY RANGE:

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location.  Pay rates are established taking into account the following factors:  federal, state, and local minimum wage requirements, the geographic location differential, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, internal employee equity, and market conditions.  Our ranges may be modified at any time.

For leveled roles (I, II, III, Senior, Lead, etc.) new hires may be slotted into a different level, either up or down, based on assessment during interview process taking into consideration experience, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.  The level may impact the salary range and these adjustments would be clarified during the offer process.

Pay Range:  $61,053 – $98,334

A list of our benefit offerings can be found on our CorVel website: CorVel Careers | Opportunities in Risk Management

In general, our opportunities will be posted for up to 1 year from date of posting, or until we have selected candidate(s) to fulfill the opening, whichever comes first.

jobs.title: Senior Vermont Claims Specialist
jobs.description_html:
The Senior Claims Specialist handles complex and high-profile Workers' Compensation claims following company standards. This role works closely with case managers and attorneys, manages subrogation, and negotiates settlements. The Senior Claims Specialist ensures the best possible outcome for the claim, meeting customer service expectations, and supporting the goals of the Claims Department and CorVel.

This is a remote position.

Vermont adjuster license required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Receives Workers’ Compensation claim, confirms policy coverage and acknowledgement of the claim
  • Determines validity and compensability of the claim by investigating and gathering information regarding the claim and files necessary documentation with state agencies
  • Establishes reserves and authorizes payments within reserving authority limits
  • Develops and manages well documented action plans with the case manager and outcomes manager to reduce overall cost of the claim
  • Coordinates early return-to-work efforts with the appropriate parties
  • Manages subrogation and litigation of claim as it applies
  • Manages potential claim recoveries of all types
  • Reports claims to the excess carrier when applicable
  • Communicates claim status with the customer and claimant
  • Adheres to client and carrier guidelines and participates in claims review as needed
  • Develops and maintains professional customer relationships
  • Complies with rules and regulations of applicable state
  • Additional duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to assist team members to develop knowledge and understanding of claims practice
  • Ability to identify, analyze and solve problems
  • Computer proficiency and technical aptitude with the ability to utilize Microsoft Office including Excel spreadsheets
  • Strong interpersonal, time management and organizational skills
  • Ability to work both independently and within a team environment
  • Knowledge of the entire claims administration, case management and cost containment solution as applicable to Workers’ Compensation

EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Vermont adjuster license required
  • Bachelor's degree or a combination of education and related experience
  • Minimum of 3 years’ industry experience and claim handling
  • Self-Insured Certificate preferred
  • State Certification or license as an experienced claims adjuster
  • Current license or certification in Workers’ Compensation must be maintained throughout employment with CorVel

PAY RANGE:

CorVel uses a market based approach to pay and our salary ranges may vary depending on your location.  Pay rates are established taking into account the following factors:  federal, state, and local minimum wage requirements, the geographic location differential, job-related skills, experience, qualifications, internal employee equity, and market conditions.  Our ranges may be modified at any time.

For leveled roles (I, II, III, Senior, Lead, etc.) new hires may be slotted into a different level, either up or down, based on assessment during interview process taking into consideration experience, qualifications, and overall fit for the role.  The level may impact the salary range and these adjustments would be clarified during the offer process.

Pay Range:  $61,053 – $98,334

jobs.description_html:
The Vice President, Carrier Partnerships, is an executive-level position and is responsible for maintaining, growing and establishing new key partnerships with Enterprise Claims carriers throughout the country. Additionally, this role is responsible for carrier stewardship, including annual in-person meetings, contract management, and renewals.

The VP, Carrier Partnerships, works closely with internal stakeholders, including Sales, EVP of Risk Management Services, Compliance Directors, and Vice President(s) of QA, Corporate Legal and other key contributors within the organization.

This is a remote position.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Maintains continuous communication with key Enterprise Claims carriers to ensure that all service expectations are identified and met
  • Pursues new carrier partnerships, while continuing to manage and build upon existing partnerships by taking a consultative approach
  • Embodies a strong executive presence and possesses comprehensive knowledge of CorVel’s suite of services along with all competitive offerings
  • Works closely with Account Managers that manage the Guaranteed Cost relationships
  • Manages contract negotiations, pricing, and implementation of carrier business, coordinating with all internal and external stakeholders
  • Conducts regular stewardship meetings to review the previous year’s performance while highlighting the value of the partnership and service impact
  • Collaborates with stakeholders to work through challenges and barriers to success
  • Proactively identifies and escalates existing or potential issues to appropriate members of the management and executive teams to address concerns before they adversely affect the partnership
  • Stays ahead of market changes and continues to build CorVel’s reputation as an industry leader
  • Responds in a timely and comprehensive manner to all issues and questions that arise
  • Travels overnight to meetings and conferences multiple times per year, as needed
  • Additional duties as assigned

    KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS:

    • Ability to understand CorVel's performance results and identify opportunities to improve outcomes and increase savings
    • Leadership skills along with thorough knowledge of CorVel’s services and offerings
    • Business acumen, coupled with enthusiasm, persistence and decorum
    • Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills
    • Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to build long-term, mutually trusting partnerships
    • Sense of urgency and ability to handle multiple competing priorities in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
    • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to build creative solutions to come to a mutually beneficial agreement
    • Highly developed organizational abilities as well as time management skills
    • Must be proficient in Microsoft Office applications
    • Ability to travel to meetings and conferences, as needed

    EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

    • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or a combination of education and equivalent experience
    • 7-10 years of progressive experience in a related field
    • Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience
