jobs.title: Project Manager - Power Distribution Solutions
jobs.description_html:
Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?

Transform the everyday with us!

The Electrification and Automation (EA) Business Unit offers the full range of energy distribution systems and solutions for all markets and through all sales channels. We provide reliable power distribution grids of today while investing into our Future Grids portfolio and applications to create the power distribution grid of the future. Our comprehensive portfolio meets the growing technical requirements of todays and tomorrow’s power grid!

We’re looking for a Project Manager to lead complex, high-impact projects from initiation through closeout. In this role, you’ll work within a matrixed organization and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver medium-voltage power distribution solutions, photovoltaic inverter projects, and automation-focused systems.

You’ll manage customer-facing projects in a fast-paced environment, balancing scope, schedule, budget, quality, and stakeholder expectations. This position offers strong opportunities for growth, aligned with Siemens’ commitment to developing people with a continuous learning mindset.

This role can be based remotely within the United States.

You’ll make a difference by:

  • Lead all phases of assigned projects—from planning to execution and final closeout.
  • Own project cost, schedule, quality, and technical performance.
  • Define project milestones and ensure alignment with master plans and timelines.
  • Communicate expectations, updates, risks, and progress clearly to team members, leadership, and customers.
  • Provide routine status reports covering scope, budget, schedule, and performance.
  • Identify project risks or issues and drive effective solutions (including resource allocation or contract adjustments).
  • Handle customer expectations throughout the entire project lifecycle.
  • Lead single- and multi-product medium-voltage solutions projects.
  • Conduct diagnostics to resolve root causes and implement corrective actions.

You’ll win us over by having the following qualifications:

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 5+ years of project management experience in the power distribution industry, focusing on medium- or high-voltage equipment/switchgear.
  • Ability to travel up to 20%, both domestically and internationally.
  • Authorization to work in the U.S. permanently without company sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret results and present recommendations to senior management and customers.
  • Proven leadership experience leading multi-disciplinary teams (program management, engineering, services, operations, logistics).
  • Demonstrated success driving and running projects in competitive technical markets.
  • Experience implementing cost-saving measures within projects.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for presenting complex information to varied audiences.
  • Experience in contract management and change management.
  • PMP certification (or willingness to obtain within one year of hire).

About Siemens:

We are a global technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. From more resource-efficient factories, resilient supply chains, and smarter buildings and grids, to sustainable transportation as well as advanced healthcare, we create technology with purpose adding real value for customers. Learn more about Siemens here.

Our Commitment to Equity and Inclusion in our Diverse Global Workforce:

We value your unique identity and perspective. We are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society, while ensuring that we attract the best talent based on qualifications, skills, and experiences. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us.

#LI-RB1


You’ll Benefit From
Siemens offers a variety of health and wellness benefits to our employees. Details regarding our benefits can be found here: https://www.benefitsquickstart.com/siemens/index.html
The pay range for this position is $91,463 - $156,794 annually with a target incentive of 10% of the base salary. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.

jobs.title: Field Service Safety Professional
jobs.description_html:
Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this by empowering customers through the combination of the real and digital worlds, improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation. We know that a business thrives when its people are thriving. That is why we put our people first. Our global, diverse team will support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?

Transform the everyday with us!

Our Power Protection & Automation field teams support the safe installation, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, energization, and service of electrical protection, control, automation, and power-distribution systems.

We are looking for a Field Service Safety Professional. This remote position will support field operations throughout the United States and requires approximately 70% travel.

You'll make a difference by:

  • Conduct scheduled and unannounced jobsite visits to identify hazards, verify controls, coach field teams, and evaluate compliance with Siemens, customer, and regulatory requirements.
  • Review job hazard analyses, pre-task and switching plans, commissioning procedures, single-line diagrams, and equipment drawings to confirm scope, energy sources, boundaries, equipment condition, and ownership.
  • Verify hazardous-energy and electrical safety controls, including equipment identification, isolation, lockout/tagout, Live-Dead-Live absence-of-voltage testing, grounding when required, boundaries, personal protective equipment, test instruments, barriers, and work-zone controls.
  • Provide safety oversight for relay and secondary-injection testing, point-to-point checks, functional trip testing, breaker operation, remote switching, temporary test connections, energization, and complex commissioning activities.
  • Monitor other high-risk work, including lifting and rigging, work at height, confined-space entry, material handling, and simultaneous operations, and exercise stop-work authority when conditions, responsibilities, or protective measures are unclear or unsafe.
  • Lead or support incident, near-miss, and electrical-event investigations; deliver field-focused training, toolbox talks, stand-downs, and coaching; and track corrective actions, recurring hazards, trends, and leading indicators.

You'll win us over by having the following qualifications:

Basic Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent and 5 or more years of construction, industrial, utility, electrical, or field-service safety experience.
  • Working knowledge of Occupational Safety and Health Administration general industry and construction requirements, electrical safe-work practices, and NFPA 70E.
  • Experience supporting electrical power-distribution equipment or protection and automation environments, including hazard recognition, inspections, job hazard analyses, energy-control verification, field coaching, and stop-work intervention.
  • Ability to interpret technical documentation, identify safety-critical conditions, and conduct incident, near-miss, and electrical-event investigations, including root cause analysis and corrective-action closure.
  • Ability to travel approximately 70% to active construction, industrial, utility, and customer facilities, including overnight and occasional off-hours work; ability to navigate stairs, ladders, uneven surfaces, equipment rooms, and outdoor areas while wearing required personal protective equipment.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in safety, environmental health and safety, electrical or engineering technology, construction management, or a related field.
  • Certified Health and Safety Technician, Associate Safety Professional, Certified Safety Professional, Occupational Hygiene and Safety Technician, or an equivalent credential.
  • Current or prior training in OSHA 30, OSHA 510/511, OSHA 500/501, NFPA 70E, First Aid/CPR/AED, or incident investigation.
  • Experience with protective-relay testing, control panels, substation automation, switchgear or breaker commissioning, electrical-system energization, and related AC/DC control and communication systems in utilities, substations, data centers, semiconductor facilities, manufacturing, renewable energy, or other high-reliability environments.

About Siemens:

We are a global technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. From more resource-efficient factories, resilient supply chains, and smarter buildings and grids to sustainable transportation and advanced healthcare, we create technology with purpose, adding real value for customers. Learn more about Siemens here.

Our Commitment to Equity and Inclusion in our Diverse Global Workforce:

We value your unique identity and perspective. We are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society, while ensuring that we attract the best talent based on qualifications, skills, and experiences. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us.


You’ll Benefit From
Siemens offers a variety of health and wellness benefits to our employees. Details regarding our benefits can be found here: https://www.benefitsquickstart.com/siemens/index.html
The pay range for this position is $74,970 - $128,520 annually with a target incentive of 5% of the base salary. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.

jobs.title: Smart Buildings Technical Sales Intern
jobs.description_html:
Smart Buildings Technical Sales Internship 

Location:  Jacksonville, FL

Undergraduate: Rising Junior 

Duration: 10 weeks
Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7, or June 14, 2027
Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/week


Smart Buildings Sales Internship 

 

Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?  

Who designs your future?  You do. 

Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you? 

Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern in Summer 2027! 

How long is the Smart Buildings Sales Internship and when can I start?

This internship is a 10-week program where you will rotate through various departments at your local branch office, focusing all on smart buildings and sustainable infrastructure.  Internship Program Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7 and June 14, 2027.

This is a hybrid sales internship supporting Building Automation, Fire & Life Safety and Security businesses, for both Solutions and Service Sales.

What is Building Automation?

Siemens Building Automation Systems is a building management system (BMS) that automatically manages and controls all systems within a building. These systems include lighting, heating, cooling, ventilation, fire detection and notification, CCTV, door and window controls, water and waste management. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. The system is designed to manage a wide range of building systems, such as HVAC, lighting, security, fire safety, and other critical building functions.

Click HERE to learn more about Siemens’ Building Automation and Control Systems.

What is the difference between Solutions & Service Sales?

The Solutions Sales Team is committed to supporting our new construction customers and will achieve booking and profit goals by developing and implementing plans to grow, develop, and manage contractor, consultant, developer, and end-user relationships; capitalize on sales opportunities within the territory; and effectively execute sophisticated deals independently within our established guidelines.

The Service Sales Team is committed to supporting our Service Agreements business for commercial building automation controls, fire/life safety and security systems. The Service Sales Team supports our Operations Team whose focus is to perform service and maintenance in large commercial buildings such as hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities.

What will I do as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern?

  • Work alongside Sales Managers and Sales Executives within the local branch office.
  • Assist the sales team with lead generation, prospecting, and account outreach.
  • Support the preparation of sales presentations, proposals, and reports.
  • Help manage CRM data by tracking leads and maintaining data accuracy.
  • Shadow sales calls and meetings to learn effective sales techniques.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (operations, other business units, departments, etc.) to support customer engagement
  • Analyze sales performance data and provide insights into driving growth.
  • Participate in team meetings and contribute creative ideas for improving sales processes.
  • Participate in sales related activities (learning how to prospect, go-to-market, build B2B relationships, on-the-job training and shadowing, etc.)

·       Rotate through our core business segments, which include Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, Security and Energy/Sustainability Systems. 

 

What will my responsibilities be as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern?

  • Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator. 
  • Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes. 
  • Help prospect for new customers and engage with existing customers on new offerings. 
  • Visit customer sites with both Solutions and Services Sales Teams. 
  • Develop value-based proposals, estimates, specifications, and presentations.
  • Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale. 
  • Attend job take-offs and turnover meetings. 
  • Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends. 

The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation. 

To apply for the Smart Buildings Sales Internship, candidates must meet the following requirements:

  • Education: Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university.
  • Majors: Pursing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Energy/Sustainability, Built Environment, Construction Management or Business Administration, Sales/Marketing with a strong technical engineering aptitude. 
  • Preferred: Participation in a school sponsored sales engineering club/organization, pursuing a professional sales certificate or similar.
  • Availability:  Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August).
  • Relocation: No relocation assistance or housing stipend is provided.  Must be willing and able to work at the branch office location and surrounding local area. 
  • Work Authorization:  Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company or school sponsorship.  This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPT.

Benefits:

The hourly pay range for this position is $24 - $28 per hour, based off of your projected graduation year.  The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.  Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program. 

#LI-ARS #NSSE26 #URDP



You’ll Benefit From
The hourly pay range for this position is 24 per hour for first time Interns or 28 per hour for returning Interns. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location. Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program.

 The Solutions Sales Team is committed to supporting our new construction customers and will achieve booking and profit goals by developing and implementing plans to grow, develop, and manage contractor, consultant, developer, and end-user relationships; capitalize on sales opportunities within the territory; and effectively execute sophisticated deals independently within our established guidelines.
 The Service Sales Team is committed to supporting our Service Agreements business for commercial building automation controls, fire/life safety and security systems. The Service Sales Team supports our Operations Team whose focus is to perform service and maintenance in large commercial buildings such as hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. 
 What will I do as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern? 
 Work alongside Sales Managers and Sales Executives within the local branch office.
 Assist the sales team with lead generation, prospecting, and account outreach.
 Support the preparation of sales presentations, proposals, and reports.
 Help manage CRM data by tracking leads and maintaining data accuracy.
 Shadow sales calls and meetings to learn effective sales techniques.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (operations, other business units, departments, etc.) to support customer engagement
 Analyze sales performance data and provide insights into driving growth.
 Participate in team meetings and contribute creative ideas for improving sales processes.
 Participate in sales related activities (learning how to prospect, go-to-market, build B2B relationships, on-the-job training and shadowing, etc.)
 · Rotate through our core business segments, which include Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, Security and Energy/Sustainability Systems. 
 What will my responsibilities be as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern? 
 Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator. 
 Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes. 
 Help prospect for new customers and engage with existing customers on new offerings. 
 Visit customer sites with both Solutions and Services Sales Teams. 
 Develop value-based proposals, estimates, specifications, and presentations. 
 Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale. 
 Attend job take-offs and turnover meetings. 
 Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends. 
 The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation. 
 To apply for the Smart Buildings Sales Internship, candidates must meet the following requirements: 
 Education: Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university. 
 Majors: Pursing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Energy/Sustainability, Built Environment, Construction Management or Business Administration, Sales/Marketing with a strong technical engineering aptitude.

jobs.title: HR Program Manager, M&A
jobs.description_html:
Siemens Digital Industries Software is a leading provider of solutions for the design, simulation, and manufacture of products across many different industries. Formula 1 cars, skyscrapers, ships, space exploration vehicles, and many of the objects we see in our daily lives are being conceived and manufactured using our Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) software.

Position Overview:

Are you ready for an exciting opportunity to play a key role in the People & Organization (P&O) function leading Merger and Acquisition projects for Siemens Digital Industries Software in a fast- paced global environment? 

At Siemens Digital Industries Software, you have an opportunity to help drive the successful on-boarding and integration of newly acquired employees into a globally distributed organization. You will work closely with many talented Siemens colleagues from around the world – Global and Country P&O functions, Corporate M&A, Finance, IT, Compliance, Legal, Facilities, Procurement – and work closely with the acquired company leaders and integration team members. This role entails the full breadth of the M&A lifecycle from due diligence through all stages of integration planning and execution. The role will be based is in the United States. 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Reporting to the P&O Director, M&A for Digital Industries Software, globally lead cross functional project planning and execution for assigned M&A projects with a focus on US based acquisitions and integrations.
  • Develop end-to-end integration project plans, workstream charters, weekly updates, project templates and documentation, audit requirements and Town Hall presentations/employee communications.
  • Collaborate with Siemens Corporate M&A team to execute on due diligence, signing and closing activities.  Identifies key findings, risks, liabilities and challenges based on the deal type and integration planning concept. 
  • Partner closely with global P&O Business Partners and Country P&O Managers on retention plans for key employees, job mapping, compensation benchmarking & alignment, benefits alignment/harmonization, organization structure, employment contracts and policies.
  • Leads P&O project meetings and coaches and guides P&O project team members throughout the life cycle of the project.  
  • Establish a high level of collaboration and alignment with HRIS/Operations/Payroll, Talent Acquisition, Compensation, Benefits, Immigration, L&D, etc.  on P&O integration concept and planning activities.
  • Ensure close collaboration and communication with multiple stakeholders across inter-dependent workstreams – IT, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications, Facilities, Procurement, etc.
  • Deliver against defined project milestones ensuring integration of all P&O processes, policies and technology including but not limited to payroll, HR data management, total rewards, talent acquisition, talent management, employment policies and compliance, employee surveys
  • Provide oversight and direction on the communications and change management strategy and employee engagement plan development.
  • Participate in global P&O projects on an ad hoc basis.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree’s is required
  • Preferably, a minimum of 3 years of experience supporting mergers and acquisitions (M&A), including conducting and/or coordinating due diligence activities, supporting transaction execution, and assisting with post-acquisition integration efforts.
  • 10+ years of experience in a variety of Human Resources/People & Organization roles for a large multi-national company.
  • 7+ years of experience in a HR/P&O business partner role preferably with multi-country experience supporting global employee populations and also integrating newly acquired employees into business functions (job mapping, compensation alignment, talent assessment, organization structures, etc).
  • 5+ years of experience supporting US-based new hire onboarding activities with strong knowledge of US employment laws and company employment policies. 
  • Working knowledge of multiple HR disciplines including benefits, compensation, payroll, talent management, talent acquisition, employment law and compliance.
  • Process oriented and data-driven, with the motivation and skills to improve workflows across many interdependent functions.
  • Strong sense of ownership and accountability to achieve successful project results.
  • Excellent project management and time management skills with the ability to be agile and pivot quickly as project and company needs change.
  • Strong ability to network across the organization and collaborate across all levels of the organization, with an ability to align with and influence key decision makers.
  • Ability to work autonomously and make thoughtful decisions quickly.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint, and HR systems and tools.
  • Scheduling flexibility is needed to work across multiple time zones to accommodate meeting schedules.
  • Ability to travel domestically in the US and occasionally for meetings in other countries


Why us?

Working at Siemens Software means flexibility - Choosing between working at home and the office at other times is the norm here. We offer great benefits and rewards, as you'd expect from a world leader in industrial software. A collection of over 377,000 minds building the future one day at a time in over 200 countries. We're dedicated to equality, and we welcome applications that reflect the diversity of the communities we work in. All employment decisions at Siemens are based on qualifications, merit, and business need. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow!

Siemens Software. Transform the Everyday with Us


#LI-PLM

#LI-REMOTE

jobs.title: Head of Product - Grid Planning
jobs.description_html:
Who are we?

Here at Siemens Grid Software, our mission is to accelerate and secure the energy transition in a sustainable and profitable way. And for that we need you! We are paving the way for autonomous grid management empowering grid operators to accelerate their digital transformation easier, faster, and at scale.

By leaving behind traditional ways of tackling the net zero challenge and embracing the powerful capabilities of software and digital technology, we turn the complexity of grids into competitive advantage. No matter where power comes from or where it goes, we make sure it makes its way at every step.

 Find out how Siemens Grid Software is decoding the future of energy.

Join our team, get inspired, and help us re-imagine the world! Transform the everyday with us!

We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking Head of Product for Grid Planning to lead one of our most strategically important domains.

This role carries a dual mandate: to build on Siemens’ decades-long legacy as a global leader in grid planning software, and to define what the next generation of planning solutions must become. The grid is fundamentally changing — driven by renewable integration, bidirectional power flows, and the rise of distributed energy resources — and utilities need planning tools that match this new reality.

You will set the product vision, own the roadmap, and work across engineering, UX, sales, and customer teams to deliver solutions that help utilities operate with greater confidence, efficiency, and resilience. This is a senior role with real strategic influence and visible impact.

This is a remote role based in the Central or Eastern U.S. Time Zones

You’ll make an impact as you:

  • Define the product vision. Own the multi-year grid planning roadmap, grounded in deep customer understanding and aligned with Siemens’ platform strategy.
  • Stay close to customers. Engage regularly with RTOs, ISO, utilities, and other industry stakeholders to surface genuine user needs and validate product direction before committing to build.
  • Drive the next generation of planning. Evolve our portfolio toward cloud-native, AI-augmented, and platform-integrated architectures — without sacrificing the analytical depth utilities rely on.
  • Shape the ecosystem. Define integration standards and API strategies that position Siemens Grid Software as the preferred platform hub for utility digital transformation.
  • Lead cross-functionally. Align engineering, UX, sales, and services around a clear and shared product direction. Drive prioritization with rigor and transparency.
  • Represent Siemens externally. Contribute to industry discourse at key events and customer forums as a credible voice in grid planning and utility technology.

You’ll win us over by having the following qualifications:

Basic qualifications:

  • Solid knowledge, credibility, and vision on how Power Utilities plan and operate their networks.
  • Experience building or scaling SaaS products, ability to create products that strongly leverage AI to build value.
  • 10+ years in product leadership and critical-thinking roles with a proven record of designing & scaling technology products.
  • Bachelor’s degree required, with a focus in business administration, finance, business informatics preferred.
  • Ability to travel minimum 50% (domestic and international)
  • Strong communication skills in business-proficient English and interculturally competent and proven track record of managing global multicultural teams.
  • Must be legally authorized for employment in the United States without the need for current or future employer-sponsored work authorization.

Create a better #TomorrowWithUs

About Siemens:

We are a global technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. From more resource-efficient factories, resilient supply chains, and smarter buildings and grids, to sustainable transportation as well as advanced healthcare, we create technology with purpose adding real value for customers.

Our Commitment to Equity and Inclusion in our Diverse Global Workforce:

We value your unique identity and perspective. We are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society, while ensuring that we attract the best talent based on qualifications, skills, and experiences. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us.

#GSWUS


You’ll Benefit From
Siemens offers a variety of health and wellness benefits to our employees. Details regarding our benefits can be found here: https://www.benefitsquickstart.com/siemens/index.html
The pay range for this position is $145,156 - $248,839 annually with a target incentive of 20% of the base salary. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager – Data Center Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description_html:
The Principal Technical Program Manager will lead complex, multi-year data center infrastructure, consolidation, migration, and technology-transformation programs across enterprise and cloud environments. 


This role is responsible for translating business and technical requirements into executable infrastructure strategies, coordinating cross-functional engineering and operational teams, and maintaining control of scope, schedule, budget, risk, quality, and stakeholder expectations. The successful candidate will combine strong technical knowledge of data center, network, security, compute, storage, virtualization, and disaster-recovery environments with senior-level program leadership. 


The position is best suited to an experienced infrastructure leader who can operate effectively in ambiguous environments, establish governance, challenge incomplete requirements, and guide programs from initial assessment and strategy through design, procurement, deployment, migration, commissioning, and operational handover. This closely reflects the candidate’s demonstrated experience managing large data center portfolios, critical migrations, network and security architecture, and enterprise infrastructure programs.  


Key Responsibilities:

Data Center Strategy and Program Leadership 

  • Lead end-to-end planning and execution of complex, multi-phase data center and critical-infrastructure programs.  

  • Develop data center consolidation, migration, modernization, capacity, resilience, and lifecycle strategies.  

  • Establish program objectives, delivery roadmaps, workstreams, milestones, dependencies, governance structures, and success criteria.  

  • Convert strategic requirements into executable project scopes, schedules, resource plans, budgets, and risk-management plans.  

  • Lead infrastructure assessments to evaluate current-state architecture, operational maturity, service resilience, capacity, technical debt, and business-continuity risks.  

  • Identify gaps between contracted scope, stated requirements, and discovered operational or technical needs.  

  • Evaluate program alternatives and clearly communicate cost, schedule, risk, operational, and technical tradeoffs to leadership.  

  • Maintain accountability for overall program performance while coordinating multiple projects, vendors, and technical disciplines.  


Data Center Design and Infrastructure Coordination 

  • Coordinate the development and review of high-level data center infrastructure architectures and design requirements.  

  • Ensure that compute, storage, virtualization, network, cybersecurity, facilities, cloud, and application requirements are incorporated into the overall solution.  

  • Facilitate technical alignment among data center architects, facilities engineers, network and security teams, platform teams, application owners, operations, and external consultants.  

  • Support active-active, primary-secondary, disaster-recovery, high-performance computing, and critical-production infrastructure strategies.  

  • Review design assumptions for availability, scalability, maintainability, redundancy, recoverability, capacity, and operational readiness.  

  • Identify infrastructure dependencies and integration requirements across network, security, compute, storage, application, and facility environments.  

  • Support the development of migration architectures, sequencing plans, coexistence strategies, rollback plans, and cutover requirements.  

The role does not replace the licensed architects or engineers responsible for detailed electrical, mechanical, structural, fire-protection, or code-compliance design. It provides technical program leadership and ensures that those disciplines are properly coordinated. 


Migration and Deployment Management 

  • Develop and govern migration frameworks for critical applications, infrastructure platforms, and data center services.  

  • Coordinate application discovery, dependency mapping, migration-wave planning, readiness reviews, cutover execution, rollback planning, and post-migration validation.  

  • Lead deployment planning for greenfield and brownfield data center environments.  

  • Ensure infrastructure, network, security, operations, facilities, and application teams are aligned before migration or production activation.  

  • Establish formal entry and exit criteria for design, build, testing, commissioning, migration, and operational handover phases.  

  • Track implementation defects, open risks, incomplete deliverables, and operational-readiness gaps through final closure.  

  • Coordinate business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning for critical services.  

The candidate’s background includes leading active-active greenfield data center deployments, establishing migration processes for more than 10,000 critical applications, and managing major infrastructure programs with substantial budgets and extended delivery schedules.  


Network, Security, and Technology Integration 

  • Provide program-level oversight for enterprise data center network and security architecture.  

  • Coordinate LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, software-defined networking, routing, firewall, remote-access, and unified-communications workstreams.  

  • Ensure network and security designs meet availability, performance, segmentation, scalability, and operational-support requirements.  

  • Facilitate coordination of routing, failover, connectivity, authentication, access-control, and security-zone requirements.  

  • Ensure cybersecurity, governance, risk, and compliance requirements are incorporated into program planning and design decisions.  

  • Guide technical teams in evaluating infrastructure standards, technology lifecycles, automation opportunities, and future-state roadmaps.  


Commercial, Procurement, and Vendor Management 

  • Support the preparation, evaluation, clarification, and negotiation of RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, SOWs, and vendor proposals.  

  • Translate technical and operational requirements into clear procurement documentation and evaluation criteria.  

  • Coordinate technical due diligence of data center operators, consultants, contractors, technology suppliers, and managed-service providers.  

  • Evaluate vendor proposals for technical compliance, delivery risk, commercial assumptions, scalability, resilience, and operational suitability.  

  • Monitor vendor performance against contractual milestones, deliverables, service levels, and quality requirements.  

  • Identify scope gaps, exclusions, assumptions, change requests, and commercial risks before they affect delivery.  

  • Support contract negotiations and change-control discussions by providing documented technical and program-impact analysis.  


Governance, Risk, and Executive Communication 

  • Establish and maintain program governance, reporting, escalation, decision-making, and change-control processes.  

  • Maintain integrated RAID logs covering risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and decisions.  

  • Track schedule, budget, scope, quality, resource capacity, benefits realization, and operational-readiness indicators.  

  • Prepare executive-level reports, decision papers, program dashboards, and recommendations.  

  • Clearly communicate complex technical issues to executive, business, operational, and nontechnical stakeholders.  

  • Escalate unresolved risks, scope conflicts, budget pressures, resource constraints, and delivery concerns in a timely manner.  

  • Facilitate steering committees, design reviews, readiness reviews, risk workshops, and executive decision meetings.  

  • Create consistent program-management processes and reusable organizational assets across portfolios and business units.  

The candidate has demonstrated experience developing governance frameworks, managing program changes and tradeoffs, coordinating subject-matter experts, and reporting schedule, budget, quality, and risk to senior leadership.  


Stakeholder and Team Leadership 

  • Build strong working relationships with CIOs, directors, senior managers, engineering leaders, application owners, operations teams, facilities organizations, procurement, finance, and external partners.  

  • Lead multidisciplinary teams without relying solely on direct reporting authority.  

  • Clarify roles, responsibilities, interfaces, decision rights, and escalation paths across program participants.  

  • Promote accountability, transparency, customer advocacy, continuous improvement, and high delivery standards.  

  • Mentor project managers, technical leads, analysts, and other program team members.  

  • Resolve conflicts constructively while protecting agreed program objectives, governance, and technical requirements.  


Required Qualifications:

 Establish formal entry and exit criteria for design, build, testing, commissioning, migration, and operational handover phases. 
 Track implementation defects, open risks, incomplete deliverables, and operational-readiness gaps through final closure. 
 Coordinate business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning for critical services. 
 The candidate’s background includes leading active-active greenfield data center deployments, establishing migration processes for more than 10,000 critical applications, and managing major infrastructure programs with substantial budgets and extended delivery schedules.

 Coordinate LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, software-defined networking, routing, firewall, remote-access, and unified-communications workstreams.

 Facilitate coordination of routing, failover, connectivity, authentication, access-control, and security-zone requirements. 
 Ensure cybersecurity, governance, risk, and compliance requirements are incorporated into program planning and design decisions. 
 Guide technical teams in evaluating infrastructure standards, technology lifecycles, automation opportunities, and future-state roadmaps.

 Support the preparation, evaluation, clarification, and negotiation of RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, SOWs, and vendor proposals. 
 Translate technical and operational requirements into clear procurement documentation and evaluation criteria. 
 Coordinate technical due diligence of data center operators, consultants, contractors, technology suppliers, and managed-service providers. 
 Evaluate vendor proposals for technical compliance, delivery risk, commercial assumptions, scalability, resilience, and operational suitability. 
 Monitor vendor performance against contractual milestones, deliverables, service levels, and quality requirements. 
 Identify scope gaps, exclusions, assumptions, change requests, and commercial risks before they affect delivery. 
 Support contract negotiations and change-control discussions by providing documented technical and program-impact analysis.

jobs.title: SkillBridge Internship – Associate Project Manager
jobs.description_html:
Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?  

Transform the everyday with us!

Our Smart Buildings help to create efficient, safe, adaptable, and responsible environments. Our aim isn’t just about improving buildings; it’s about creating perfect places that improve people’s lives. 

This opportunity is unique to active-duty US Military Service members with formal approval to participate as a SkillBridge Intern in collaboration with Vets2PM’s authorized SkillBridge program.  

You will gain hands-on experience during your internship and will have the opportunity to join (upon successful completion of the internship) one of the world's leading technology companies.

Curious to see how Siemens recognizes the Military Community? CLICK HERE: Military Video

Our Three Main Business Groups that you could be assigned to:

  • Building Automation:  HVAC Controls, Lighting Controls, & Mechanical/Electrical Services
  • Fire/Life Safety:  Fire Alarm, Mass/Emergency Communication, and Sprinkler/Suppression
  • Security: Integrated Surveillance and Access Controls

Technical Project Management

When supporting our Project Management teams, you will coordinate and deliver multiple, simultaneous Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, or Integrated Security projects of various complexities in commercial buildings. You will also strategically manage fiscal responsibility for all project facets, including project billing, job cost reporting, and overall customer satisfaction.

Responsibilities and learning opportunities include but are not limited to:

  • Review project contracts, specs, and drawings to establish intent
  • Develop and maintain project schedules, coordinate team needs, and identify time-sensitive installations
  • Manage supply requisitions and oversee materials procurement
  • Review plans, participate in cost reviews, and assist in subcontractor contracting
  • Conduct orientation for technicians, provide project documentation, and track resources
  • Document events impacting schedule, scope, and efficiency
  • Pursue change-order opportunities and coordinate billing
  • Schedule commissioning resources and provide documentation
  • Expedite mark-ups for as-built development
  • Complete project-specific close-out documentation

Desired Military Experience, Backgrounds and/or Aptitude, but not limited to: 

  • Civil Engineering (HVAC & Electrician)/ Gas Turbine Electricians 
  • Mechanical/Electrical/Electronic Systems 
  • Automation/Integration Technicians 
  • Nuclear Engineering/Power/Energy & Nuclear Plant Operator 
  • Satellite/Radar Systems 
  • Comm Techs 
  • Fire Control Navaids 
  • Submarine Electronics/Computer Techs 
  • Avionics Systems & more! 

You’ll make an immediate impact by having the following qualifications:

Basic Qualifications:

  • Only active military personnel will be considered for this internship and program acceptance requires military approval
    • Selected candidates will continue to be paid under their current wage/benefits provided by the US Military and will not be paid by Siemens directly throughout internship participation
  • High school diploma or state-recognized GED required
  • Demonstrated experience and/or applied knowledge/aptitude in the following:
    • Electro-mechanical aptitude
    • Technical experience supporting mechanical, electrical, thermodynamic, hydraulic, mechatronic, construction (MEP) or other related systems
    • Project management experience to include project scope, scheduling, documentation, resource allocation and fiscal responsibility
    • Experience using Microsoft Office applications
    • Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively (verbal & written)
    • Demonstrated ability to interface with customers and collaborate with team members
    • Ability to work on-site and travel within assigned local area as needed
  • Qualified applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States
  • Must be 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license with limited violations

Preferred Qualifications:

  • U.S. Military experience as an E5 or above (Navy, Air Force, Army, Marines, Coast Guard, Space Force, National Guard, Reserves)
  • Associate or bachelor’s degree
  • Experience in demand-side energy services or Certified Energy Manager preferred
  • Familiarity or experience with engineering HVAC, Building Automation, Fire Alarm, or Security systems

Ready to create your own journey? Join us today.

About Siemens: 

We are a global technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, transport, and healthcare. From more resource-efficient factories, resilient supply chains, and smarter buildings and grids, to sustainable transportation as well as advanced healthcare, we create technology with purpose adding real value for customers. Learn more about Siemens here.

Our Commitment to Equity and Inclusion in our Diverse Global Workforce

We value your unique identity and perspective. We are fully committed to providing equitable opportunities and building a workplace that reflects the diversity of society, while ensuring that we attract the best talent based on qualifications, skills, and experiences. We welcome you to bring your authentic self and transform the everyday with us.

Position Location: This role is a US based remote position.


Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. We are improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?


Our Smart Buildings help to create efficient, safe, adaptable, and responsible environments. Our aim isn’t just about improving buildings; it’s about creating perfect places that improve people’s lives.

Transform the everyday with us!


As the Vertical Sales Executive - Higher Education (Building Automation), you will identify, develop, and win large-scale capital projects valued at $3M+ across colleges and universities. This is a strategic, quota-carrying hunting role focused on creating opportunities before they reach procurement, building executive-level relationships, and leading complex pursuits involving building automation, digitalization, energy infrastructure, and smart campus modernization.

Successful candidates are energized by proactive prospecting, uncovering customer needs, influencing decision makers, shaping projects before RFP release, and orchestrating cross-functional teams to secure transformational projects. Higher Education experience is valued, but demonstrated success hunting and closing complex technical opportunities is the primary requirement.


As the Vertical Sales Executive – Higher Education (Building Automation), you will:

  • Identify, qualify, and pursue new capital-project opportunities valued at $3M+ across an assigned national or regional portfolio of Higher Education accounts.
  • Build a robust, self-generated pipeline through targeted prospecting, market intelligence, industry networks, construction and capital-plan signals, partner relationships, and direct executive outreach.
  • Create and advance opportunities before formal procurement or RFP release by shaping customer priorities, influencing solution strategy, and positioning Siemens as the preferred partner.
  • Lead complex pursuits from initial identification through qualification, solution development, executive alignment, commercial strategy, proposal, negotiation, and project award.
  • Develop executive relationships with university leaders across Facilities, Finance, Operations, Sustainability, Procurement, Research, and the C-suite.
  • Build compelling business cases that connect automation, digitalization, energy performance, resilience, deferred maintenance, and lifecycle outcomes to institutional priorities.
  • Orchestrate Siemens Area teams, operations leaders, technical specialists, Digital and Automation resources, partners, and executive sponsors around a clear win strategy.
  • Position Siemens building automation, Building X, digital services, energy optimization, infrastructure modernization, and related smart-campus capabilities as an integrated customer solution.
  • Own account and pursuit strategies while collaborating effectively within Siemens' matrixed sales model and respecting local customer relationships and execution responsibilities.
  • Maintain disciplined pipeline, forecast, probability, next-step, and customer-engagement data in Siemens sales systems.
  • Use AI-enabled tools and data sources to accelerate account research, stakeholder mapping, outreach preparation, opportunity qualification, and pursuit planning.
  • Represent Siemens at targeted customer meetings, conferences, industry associations, and partner events.
  • Collaborate with delivery and operations teams to ensure commitments made during the sales process are executable, profitable, and aligned with customer expectations.

You will make an impact with these qualifications:

Basic Qualifications

  • 8+ years of quota-carrying sales experience in building automation, controls, energy services, infrastructure modernization, performance contracting, digital buildings, or similarly complex technical solutions
  • Demonstrated success originating, developing, and closing large capital or enterprise opportunities valued at $3M+
  • Proven history of new-logo acquisition, proactive pipeline generation, and advancing opportunities without relying primarily on inbound demand or inherited accounts
  • Experience leading long-cycle, multi-stakeholder pursuits involving executive decision makers, engineering, operations, finance, procurement, and external partners
  • Ability to establish credibility with both technical and executive audiences and translate complex capabilities into measurable business outcomes
  • Strong financial and commercial acumen, including value-based selling, business-case development, forecasting, negotiation, and margin discipline
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional pursuit teams and influencing contributors without direct authority
  • Ability and willingness to travel approximately 50% based on customer, pursuit, conference, and team needs
  • Must be 21 years of age and possess a valid driver's license with limited violations; must meet eligibility requirements to participate in Siemens' fleet vehicle program
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Current or prior Siemens sales experience, including working knowledge of Siemens Building Automation, Digital Buildings, Building X, energy, or related Smart Infrastructure offerings
  • Experience selling directly to colleges, universities, healthcare systems, government agencies, or similarly complex institutional customers
  • Experience with performance contracting, capital planning, deferred maintenance, central utility or energy infrastructure, modernization programs, or multi-building portfolios
  • Familiarity with consultant, architect, engineer, general contractor, mechanical contractor, electrical contractor, and partner-influence channels
  • Understanding of Higher Education capital approval, funding, procurement, governance, and consensus-driven decision making
  • Experience with Siemens sales and project governance processes, including SieSales and relevant milestones
  • Knowledge of digital building platforms, analytics, AI-enabled building services, energy optimization, and recurring digital-service models

 Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. We are improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?
 Our Smart Buildings help to create efficient, safe, adaptable, and responsible environments. Our aim isn’t just about improving buildings; it’s about creating perfect places that improve people’s lives.
 Transform the everyday with us! 
 As the Vertical Sales Executive - Higher Education (Building Automation) , you will identify, develop, and win large-scale capital projects valued at $3M+ across colleges and universities. This is a strategic, quota-carrying hunting role focused on creating opportunities before they reach procurement, building executive-level relationships, and leading complex pursuits involving building automation, digitalization, energy infrastructure, and smart campus modernization.
 Successful candidates are energized by proactive prospecting, uncovering customer needs, influencing decision makers, shaping projects before RFP release, and orchestrating cross-functional teams to secure transformational projects. Higher Education experience is valued, but demonstrated success hunting and closing complex technical opportunities is the primary requirement.
 As the Vertical Sales Executive – Higher Education (Building Automation), you will: 
 Identify, qualify, and pursue new capital-project opportunities valued at $3M+ across an assigned national or regional portfolio of Higher Education accounts.
 Build a robust, self-generated pipeline through targeted prospecting, market intelligence, industry networks, construction and capital-plan signals, partner relationships, and direct executive outreach.
 Create and advance opportunities before formal procurement or RFP release by shaping customer priorities, influencing solution strategy, and positioning Siemens as the preferred partner.
 Lead complex pursuits from initial identification through qualification, solution development, executive alignment, commercial strategy, proposal, negotiation, and project award.
 Develop executive relationships with university leaders across Facilities, Finance, Operations, Sustainability, Procurement, Research, and the C-suite.
 Build compelling business cases that connect automation, digitalization, energy performance, resilience, deferred maintenance, and lifecycle outcomes to institutional priorities.
 Orchestrate Siemens Area teams, operations leaders, technical specialists, Digital and Automation resources, partners, and executive sponsors around a clear win strategy.
 Position Siemens building automation, Building X, digital services, energy optimization, infrastructure modernization, and related smart-campus capabilities as an integrated customer solution.
 Own account and pursuit strategies while collaborating effectively within Siemens' matrixed sales model and respecting local customer relationships and execution responsibilities.
 Maintain disciplined pipeline, forecast, probability, next-step, and customer-engagement data in Siemens sales systems.
 Use AI-enabled tools and data sources to accelerate account research, stakeholder mapping, outreach preparation, opportunity qualification, and pursuit planning.
 Represent Siemens at targeted customer meetings, conferences, industry associations, and partner events.
 Collaborate with delivery and operations teams to ensure commitments made during the sales process are executable, profitable, and aligned with customer expectations.
 You will make an impact with these qualifications: 
 Basic Qualifications 
 8+ years of quota-carrying sales experience in building automation, controls, energy services, infrastructure modernization, performance contracting, digital buildings, or similarly complex technical solutions
 Demonstrated success originating, developing, and closing large capital or enterprise opportunities valued at $3M+
 Proven history of new-logo acquisition, proactive pipeline generation, and advancing opportunities without relying primarily on inbound demand or inherited accounts
 Experience leading long-cycle, multi-stakeholder pursuits involving executive decision makers, engineering, operations, finance, procurement, and external partners
 Ability to establish credibility with both technical and executive audiences and translate complex capabilities into measurable business outcomes
 Strong financial and commercial acumen, including value-based selling, business-case development, forecasting, negotiation, and margin discipline
 Experience coordinating cross-functional pursuit teams and influencing contributors without direct authority
 Ability and willingness to travel approximately 50% based on customer, pursuit, conference, and team needs
 Must be 21 years of age and possess a valid driver's license with limited violations; must meet eligibility requirements to participate in Siemens' fleet vehicle program
 Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Current or prior Siemens sales experience, including working knowledge of Siemens Building Automation, Digital Buildings, Building X, energy, or related Smart Infrastructure offerings
 Experience selling directly to colleges, universities, healthcare systems, government agencies, or similarly complex institutional customers
 Experience with performance contracting, capital planning, deferred maintenance, central utility or energy infrastructure, modernization programs, or multi-building portfolios
 Familiarity with consultant, architect, engineer, general contractor, mechanical contractor, electrical contractor, and partner-influence channels
 Understanding of Higher Education capital approval, funding, procurement, governance, and consensus-driven decision making
 Experience with Siemens sales and project governance processes, including SieSales and relevant milestones
 Knowledge of digital building platforms, analytics, AI-enabled building services, energy optimization, and recurring digital-service models

jobs.title: Building Automation Solutions Sales Intern
jobs.description_html:
Smart Buildings Automation Solution Sales Internship 

Location:  Pensacola, Florida area office

Undergraduate: Rising Sophomore or Junior

Duration: 10 weeks
Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7, or June 14, 2027
Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/week

 

Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?  

Who designs your future?  You do. 

Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you? 


Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Building Automation Solution Sales Intern in Summer 2027! 


How long is the Building Automation Solutions Sales Internship and when can I start?

This internship is a 10-week program where you will rotate through various departments at your local branch office, focusing all on smart buildings and sustainable infrastructure.  Internship Program Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7 and June 14, 2027.

What is Building Automation?

Siemens Building Automation Systems is a building management system (BMS) that automatically manages and controls all systems within a building. These systems include lighting, heating, cooling, ventilation, fire detection and notification, CCTV, door and window controls, water and waste management. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. The system is designed to manage a wide range of building systems, such as HVAC, lighting, security, fire safety, and other critical building functions.

Click HERE to learn more about Siemens’ Building Automation and Control Systems.


What is Building Automation Solutions Sales?

The Building Automation Solutions Sales Team is committed to supporting our new construction customers and will achieve booking and profit goals by developing and implementing plans to grow, develop, and manage contractor, consultant, developer, and end-user relationships; capitalize on sales opportunities within the territory; and effectively execute sophisticated deals independently within our established guidelines. Our Sales Executives are ambassadors of quality Siemens technology, products and services. 
 

What will I do as a Building Automation Solutions Sales Intern?

  • Work alongside Sales Managers and Sales Executives within the local branch office.
  • Assist the sales team with lead generation, prospecting, and account outreach.
  • Support the preparation of sales presentations, proposals, and reports.
  • Help manage CRM data by tracking leads and maintaining data accuracy.
  • Shadow sales calls and meetings to learn effective sales techniques.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (operations, other business units, departments, etc.) to support customer engagement
  • Analyze sales performance data and provide insights into driving growth.
  • Participate in team meetings and contribute creative ideas for improving sales processes.
  • Participate in sales related activities (learning how to prospect, go-to-market, build B2B relationships, on-the-job training and shadowing, etc.)
  • Rotate through our core business segments, which include Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, Security and Energy/Sustainability Systems. 
 

What will my responsibilities be as a Building Automation Solutions Sales Intern?

  • Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator. 
  • Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes. 
  • Help prospect for new customers and engage with existing customers on new offerings. 
  • Visit customer sites with both Solutions and Services Sales Teams. 
  • Develop value-based proposals, estimates, specifications, and presentations.
  • Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale. 
  • Attend job take-offs and turnover meetings. 
  • Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends. 

The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation. 


To apply for the Building Automation Solutions Sales Internship, candidates must meet the following requirements:

  • Education: Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university.
  • Majors: Pursing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Energy/Sustainability, Built Environment, Construction Management or Business Administration, Sales/Marketing with a strong technical engineering aptitude. 
  • Preferred: Participation in a school sponsored sales engineering club/organization, pursuing a professional sales certificate or similar.
  • Earliest Graduation Date: December 2027
  • Availability:  Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August).
  • Relocation: No relocation assistance or housing stipend is provided.  Must be willing and able to work at the branch office location and surrounding local area. 
  • Work Authorization:  Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company or school sponsorship.  This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPT.

Benefits:

The hourly pay range for this position is $24 - $28 per hour, based off of your projected graduation year.  The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.  Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program. 

#LI-ARS #URDP #NSSE26

 



You’ll Benefit From
The hourly pay range for this position is 24 per hour for first time Interns or 28 per hour for returning Interns. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location. Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program.

jobs.title: Senior Building Automation Design Engineer
jobs.description_html:
Position Location: This role is a hybrid role.

Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. We are improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?

Our Smart Buildings help to create efficient, safe, adaptable, and responsible environments. Our aim isn’t just about improving buildings; it’s about creating perfect places that improve people’s lives.

Transform the everyday with us!


Building Automation Design Engineers create unique design solutions to meet specific customer requirements for commercial building automation systems in new and existing facilities. Building Automation Design Engineers also make recommendations for productivity improvements and cost reductions to increase customer satisfaction and job profitability.


As a Building Automation Design Engineer, you will:

  • Understand project requirements and design building automation solutions for higher education and K–12 education facilities, data centers, hospitals, pharmaceutical facilities, high-rise buildings, and lab facilities.
  • Demonstrate expertise in engineering and contracting processes, with a strong grasp of submittal requirements and documentation standards essential for project success.
  • Attend internal and external meetings to support potential opportunities and contribute technical details to project designs; meetings can be held at project sites, contractor offices and/or Siemens area offices.
  • Prepare and/or work with an engineer to prepare design documents, including mechanical system layouts, electrical drawings, system integration, bills of materials, sequences of operations, valve and damper schedules, and DDC panel layouts.
  • Design building automation network architecture to support operator workstations, DDC field panels, and third-party integration devices connected through Modbus, Siemens APOGEE, Desigo or BACnet.
  • Analyze plans, construction contract specifications, and codes to determine project requirements and risks.
  • Design building and space pressurization solutions, chiller and boiler plant sequencing control, etc.
  • Prepare engineering re-estimates and follow up with appropriate sales and management to ensure understanding of and satisfaction with job scope.
  • Perform quality assurance; peer-review engineering documents. 
 

You will make an impact with these qualifications:

Basic Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or state-recognized GED
  • 5+ years of experience in building automation (HVAC controls) design
  • Ability to travel up to 35%
  • Demonstrated ability to design large and complex jobs with some deviation using standard tools, products, and practices
  • Demonstrated knowledge of industry engineering fundamentals and business operations
  • Demonstrated proficiency in engineering design software or drafting tools such as AutoCAD or Microsoft Visio 
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company sponsorship
  • Position will be hybrid with visits to the local area office, contractor

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Associate or Bachelor’s Degree
  • 7+ years of building automation (HVAC controls) design experience

 Location: Miami area office, located in Miramar, Florida
 Undergraduate : Rising Sophomore or Junior
 Duration: 10 weeks
 Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7, or June 14, 2027
 Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/week
 Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?  
 Who designs your future? You do. 
 Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you? 
 Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Smart Buildings Fire & Life Safety Sales Intern in Summer 2027! 
 What is Smart Buildings Fire & Life Safety? 
 Fire protection systems from Siemens help keep buildings safer over their entire lifecycle, from construction through expansion, for a better tomorrow. When something matters to you, you want to give it the best possible protection. From safeguarding employees to protecting business continuity, you need a total fire and life safety partner.
 Siemens Fire and Life Safety Services and Solutions offer an innovative portfolio, backed by our certified technicians whose expertise in codes, regulations, trends, and technologies helps protect people’s lives and ensure the safety of buildings and their assets. Our comprehensive portfolio of fire panels, detection, and management stations meet the global needs of small-to-large or simple-to-complex applications.
 Click HERE to learn more about Siemens Fire Safety products and solutions.
 What will I do as a Smart Buildings Fire & Life Safety Sales Intern? 
 Work alongside Sales Managers and Sales Executives within the local branch office.
 Assist the sales team with lead generation, prospecting, and account outreach.
 Support the preparation of sales presentations, proposals, and reports.
 Help manage CRM data by tracking leads and maintaining data accuracy.
 Shadow sales calls and meetings to learn effective sales techniques.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (operations, other business units, departments, etc.) to support customer engagement
 Analyze sales performance data and provide insights into driving growth.
 Participate in team meetings and contribute creative ideas for improving sales processes.
 Participate in sales related activities (learning how to prospect, go-to-market, build B2B relationships, on-the-job training and shadowing, etc.)
 · Rotate through our core business segments, which include Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, Security and Energy/Sustainability Systems. 
 What will my responsibilities be as a Smart Buildings Fire & Life Safety Sales Intern? 
 Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator. 
 Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes. 
 Help prospect for new customers and engage with existing customers on new offerings. 
 Visit customer sites with both Solutions and Services Sales Teams. 
 Develop value-based proposals, estimates, specifications, and presentations. 
 Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale. 
 Attend job take-offs and turnover meetings. 
 Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends. 
 The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation. 
 To apply for the Smart Buildings Fire & Life Safety Sales Internship, candidates must meet the following requirements: 
 Education: Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university. 
 Majors: Pursing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Energy/Sustainability, Built Environment, Construction Management or Business Administration, Sales/Marketing with a strong technical engineering aptitude. 
 Preferred: Participation in a school sponsored sales engineering club/organization, pursuing a professional sales certificate or similar.
 Earliest Graduation Date: May 2028
 Availability: Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August).
 Relocation: No relocation assistance or housing stipend is provided. Must be willing and able to work at the branch office location and surrounding local area. 
 Eligible candidate must be located within 50 miles of office location with access to a reliable vehicle, as this role does not provide transportation, housing or relocation support.
 Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company or school sponsorship. This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPT.
 Benefits: 
 The hourly pay range for this position is $24 - $28 per hour, based off of your projected graduation year. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location. Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program. 
 #LI-ARS #NSSE26 #URDP
 You’ll Benefit From 
The hourly pay range for this position is 24 per hour for first time Interns or 28 per hour for returning Interns. The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location. Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program.
